content:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-20
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Evan Chen, Priya Kapoor (Redwood) + Carlos Mendes, Lena Ortiz, Mark Wu (Haven Logistics)

Summary:
Quick renewal/expansion check-in—Haven nearing contract renewal (Sept 2027) and looking to add dedicated capacity for their freight routing/QA models plus expansion into EU region (Paris). Discussed pricing tiers, SOC2/KMS questions, and scheduling a dedicated benchmark run. Redwood AE + SE to send updated pricing and runbook; customer to confirm benchmark date and procurement contacts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan Chen: Hey everyone, uh thanks for making time. This is Evan from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Priya our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Carlos Mendes: Morning — good, Evan. Thanks. Busy week but good.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Yep hi all.
[00:18] Mark Wu: Hi — thanks for setting this up.
[00:22] Evan Chen: Cool. Quick agenda: renewal timeline, capacity needs (you mentioned 8x A100 earlier), additional region request for Paris, and then security/compliance bits. We'll finish with next steps for pricing and a benchmark window. Sound good?
[00:34] Carlos Mendes: Sounds good. We're trying to lock in numbers so procurement can start the SOW. Renewal is Sept 15 so we have a little time.
[00:41] Evan Chen: Great. Can you recap current usage and why the 8x ask?
[00:45] Carlos Mendes: Yeah. So currently we're on a shared hosted plan — it's fine for dev but our production routing is hitting tail latency during peak loads. We saw 95th latency spikes around 800-1,200ms and we're losing throughput. Also want to move to dedicated to get consistent throughput for batch reranks. We ran a perf test last month but it wasn't on dedicated so numbers were noisy.
[01:10] Lena Ortiz: Also, we have data residency reqs for EU customers, so we need a Paris region for EU customers. Right now everything is in us-west and we have to mask some PII, but ideally we'd host inference close to EU to reduce latency and satisfy contract.
[01:26] Priya Kapoor: Quick clarifying q — when you say 8x A100, is that equivalent to eight A100 nodes or are you thinking a mix? Sometimes teams pick a mix of A100 + A10G for cost.
[01:36] Carlos Mendes: We asked for 8x A100 because of our peak QPS for the ensemble models; but we're open to recommendations if Redwood thinks quantization or batching can solve it at lower cost.
[01:49] Evan Chen: For sure. Priya, do you want to speak to the performance side?
[01:52] Priya Kapoor: Yeah. So on Dedicated, we usually see a 2-4x improvement in p95 tail compared to shared due to isolated pools and predictable batching. For Haven specifically, if you keep the same model family but pin to a dedicated 8x A100 pool and enable prefix KV cache (we sometimes heard people call it KV cash in transcriptions, ha), you'll likely see the latency drop into the 200-400ms p95 range depending on sequence length.
[02:18] Carlos Mendes: That's promising. Our sequences average 256 tokens but occasionally spike to 1k for longer context. How does the runtime handle long KV cache?
[02:26] Priya Kapoor: We manage KV cache in the runtime with smart eviction and sharding across GPUs. For those longer sequences, we can also recommend a model variant with optimized attention kernels — sometimes called a LongSeq variant — which reduces memory pressure. We also have quantization profiles that are safe for your evals; we can share recommendations after a quick eval.
[02:46] Mark Wu: On the pricing side, can you outline how the committed capacity works? We looked at the current committed monthly pricing but wanted to see incremental pricing for an 8x pool plus an extra region.
[02:57] Evan Chen: Sure. High level: there's a committed monthly fee for Redwood Dedicated which reserves the GPU pool; then usage is metered on top for bursting and token delta. For an 8x A100 pool, the blended monthly commit shifts the unit economics down versus per-request hosted. Adding a region (Paris) is an additional reserve and footprint cost — roughly 20-25% of the US pool price, ballpark. We'll put exact numbers in the proposal.
[03:23] Carlos Mendes: Ballpark is fine now, but procurement wants a firm quote soon.
[03:27] Evan Chen: Understood— we'll get you a formal renewal + expansion proposal by Friday (2027-07-22).
[03:33] Lena Ortiz: Great. On security - we need SOC2 Type II evidence, KMS / HSM integration for customer keys, and audit log detail. Also SSO/SAML mapping for role-based access.
[03:45] Priya Kapoor: We can definitely provide SOC2 summary and the audit log formats. For KMS, Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS providers; the on-prem HSM flow is a bit more bespoke, but we have a pattern. We'll share the KMS integration notes and a dedicated deployment runbook.
[04:01] Mark Wu: Is there any additional attestation we need for EU data? Data residency plus deletion certs?
[04:07] Priya Kapoor: We have data residency controls per region and can provide deletion proofs/log entries from the audit logs. There is a short lead time to spin up the Paris region as dedicated — typically 2-3 weeks once contracts and payment are in place, sometimes faster depending on capacity.
[04:22] Carlos Mendes: Okay that timeline works. Procurement will want the Paris region start date in the SOW.
[04:27] Evan Chen: We'll include that as an estimate and mark firm start contingent on payment and capacity availability.
[04:32] Carlos Mendes: About benchmarks — you mentioned doing a dedicated run. What's involved and how long?
[04:37] Priya Kapoor: The dedicated benchmark is a 1-2 day exercise. We allocate a reserved pool and run your workload (you can provide a representative trace or prompt set). We measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput. Results typically come back same day; then we do a short follow-up to go over tradeoffs like quantization. Customer provides redacted prompts and expected SLA criteria.
[04:58] Carlos Mendes: We can provide a trace. Would prefer week of July 26.
[05:02] Evan Chen: Great — we'll tentatively schedule that and Carlos you'll confirm the exact day.
[05:06] Mark Wu: On the renewal length, procurement prefers a 12-month extension with an option to expand after six months. Are there discounts for annual commits?
[05:14] Evan Chen: Yes, annual commits typically have a discount — standard tiers are 10% for 12-month, higher for multi-year commitments. For Dedicated we can also tier pricing based on committed GPU count. We'll put multiple term options in the proposal.
[05:28] Carlos Mendes: One concern internally: if we commit to 8x A100 and usage later falls, is there flexibility to downsize?
[05:36] Priya Kapoor: We have contractual options — some customers buy a baseline commit and then scale up with short-term burst pools. There are also rebalancing windows semi-annually. We'll surface the exact contract language in the proposal so procurement has visibility.
[05:52] Lena Ortiz: Also need to confirm whether logs/audit will include token-level cost breakup for our billing reconciliation.
[05:58] Evan Chen: Yes, Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. We can give you a sample export and a dashboard snapshot.
[06:06] Carlos Mendes: Are there any known limitations with your on-prem offering for air-gapped sites? We have one client in Nordics that requires on-prem.
[06:15] Priya Kapoor: On-prem is available; the control plane is usually a private control plane option and models can be packaged. Air-gapped has a longer lead time for validations and we usually do a separate security review. It's doable but it's a bigger project.
[06:28] Mark Wu: Understood. For now it's not in scope for renewal but good to know.
[06:31] Evan Chen: Quick note: you mentioned SageAI as a competitor in earlier threads. Do you have any follow up on why you might pick Redwood vs them?
[06:39] Carlos Mendes: Mostly runtime predictability and the batching/cache features sounded better with Redwood. SageAI's offering was cheaper but had more variability in tail latencies. Also Redwood's rollback/fallback policies are attractive for the teams running production.
[06:53] Priya Kapoor: Glad that came through. We also provide tooling for quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets — that often helps customers during model rollouts.
[07:03] Lena Ortiz: One technical Q — how do you handle model variants? We plan to run two model variants in prod for A/B testing and need consistent routing.
[07:12] Priya Kapoor: We support model version pinning and rollout policies such as canary, A/B, and automatic fallback. Routing policies can be based on latency SLO, region, or customer tier.
[07:22] Evan Chen: Okay, let's wrap into next steps — Evan will send formal proposal and pricing; Priya will share security artifacts and the dedicated deployment checklist; Carlos will confirm benchmark day and procurement contacts. Anything else?
[07:34] Carlos Mendes: One more—can you include a short appendix on fallback policies and what happens if a region is constrained? Our ops team asked about automatic fallback to US versus degraded mode.
[07:44] Evan Chen: Yes — we'll add a small appendix about smart routing and graceful degradation: auto-fallback to compatible model variants or region-based fallbacks with tiered latency SLOs.
[07:53] Mark Wu: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[07:56] Lena Ortiz: Thanks.
[07:58] Evan Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up Friday with the proposal.
[08:02] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: some product names transcribed oddly (RedWood Infrence vs Redwood Inference), and occasional filler words. Speakers occasionally overlap.

Recap / Next steps (chat-style):
- Evan: proposal + pricing for 8x A100 + Paris region by 2027-07-22.
- Priya: dedicated deployment checklist, SOC2 & KMS docs by 2027-07-21.
- Carlos: confirm benchmark date (week of 2027-07-26) and procurement leads by 2027-07-23.

Attachments referenced: short deck (link: https://redwood.ai/decks/haven-renewal), benchmark spreadsheet (link: internal), SOC2 summary (will be attached in follow-up).

End of transcript.
